mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to non-triggered periods at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces revenue growth for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly different from zero.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly greater than zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 0.1 percentage points for six consecutive months, despite steady GDP growth (GDPC1), indicates structural labor market slack without macroeconomic contraction, which historically coincides with stable or rising equity valuations over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises < 0.1pp for 6 consecutive months AND GDPC1 > 0% YoY
regime_hint: structural labor slack with economic growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly greater than zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for eight consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly different from zero.
